Stanford is trying to fight the good fight in a rebuild under new head coach Tavita Pritchard, but at 3-4 with only one home game left, it's in big trouble if it loses. NC State vs Stanford: Quick Hits Why does Stanford need this? Three straight road games follow this, but that includes a trip up the road to Cal. Yeah, Stanford's offense was putrid in the four losses. One of those came against a nasty Duke defense Durham, and the other three losses were to Miami, Notre Dame, and a Wake Forest team whose only loss is to the Hurricanes. This is one of those focus-test moments for the ACC team from the Eastern Time Zone. This will end around 2 am NC State time, and while these are college kids who can certainly stay awake, the rhythm will be thrown off. NC State vs Stanford Prediction, Betting Lines Don't just blow this off as a layup win for NC State before getting back on the plane to go deal with bigger and better things. The Wolfpack have had to deal with a whole ton of adversity this season, and they keep coming back, but it's 0-2 on the road, and Stanford is 3-1 at home, with that one loss coming to Miami. NC State doesn't have the pass rush to overwhelm the Cardinal backfield, but it'll be just okay enough to get out with a tough late-night win. away.headline: NC State vs. Stanford injury report: Duke Scott among many players out
away.blurb: Yousef Mugharbil joined the out-for-season list after the injury he suffered against Louisville, which is a bummer for a guy who has already been through a lot to get back to a point where he’s making an impact on the field. Jimarion McCrimon isn’t listed at all on the report this week, so that’s a positive development, but Kamen Smith is questionable again. Working with a patchwork line is a little easier against the likes of Stanford than Wake or Louisville, at least. Has NC State’s injury situation improved after a week off? No, not really. In addition to missing at least two starting linemen, State will again be without running back Duke Scott, so that’s unfortunate. Not as unfortunate as the Pack’s dilapidated ground game, but not far off. Stanford’s most notable injured player is linebacker Matt Rose, who was a second-team All-ACC player in 2025 after racking up 106 tackles. He hasn’t played in a game for the Cardinal since the last week of September.

away.headline: Stanford Injury Report Ahead of Season-Defining Matchup With NC State
away.blurb: But the program needs to get by without some key players. Ahead of the matchup, the ACC released official injury reports for this week. Stanford has multiple players still listed out, including linebacker Matt Rose and defensive back Brandon Nicholson. He has played at an elite level when healthy, but it is still to be disclosed how long he will be out. Stanford needs him back desperately to improve linebacker depth and production. Rose is the leader of the defense, and his presence elevates everyone around him. He's set to miss a significant amount of time, and it is highly possible that he will not return this season, putting the program in a tough spot. After Collin Wright missed time with an injury of his own last season, Nicholson shined and proved himself as a key player for the defense. Defensive backs Lonnie McAllister III and Chris Garland are questionable, while Lasiah Jackson is probable. NC State will be down some key stars as well. Running back Jayden Scott, defensive back Tristan Teasdell and tight end Vander Ploog headline the list of injured NC State players. Scott, NC State's leading rusher, has 62 carries for 358 yards and four touchdowns this season. With him out, it will be interesting to see how the Wolfpack's offense attacks. Wide receiver Jojo Trader and offensive tackle Kamen Smith are listed as questionable for the Wolfpack. If they return, they will provide a big boost. This game is big for both teams. For Stanford, a win puts them back at .500 and digs them out of a massive hole when it comes to returning to a bowl game. They would reach four wins, which is their total from last season, and would have a path to reaching a bowl game. That path evaporates with a loss. Starting QB CJ Bailey returning to NC State for 2026 season
away.blurb: Bailey would have been one of the top quarterbacks available had he entered the transfer portal, but the two-year starter opted to stay put -- a boon for a Wolfpack team looking to build on a strong finish to the 2025 season. The Miami, Florida, native was rumored to be a top target for several schools looking for quarterbacks in his home state, but will return to an NC State team that will now have far higher aspirations following an 8-5 campaign that ended with wins in four of its past five games. Starting QB CJ Bailey returning to NC State for 2026 season - ABC11 Raleigh-Durham 24/7 Live Raleigh Durham Fayetteville Surrounding Area SPORTS Share Follow ABC11 on Google NC State will retain starting quarterback CJ Bailey for the 2026 season, he announced on social media. Thrust into the starting role as a true freshman after a season-ending injury to Grayson McCall, Bailey blossomed into one of the more dynamic QBs in the ACC. In 2025, he threw for 3,105 yards, rushed for 215 more, and totaled 31 touchdowns, while leading NC State to a win in Union Home Mortgage Gasparilla Bowl. ESPN analysts predict Michigan-Indiana, weigh in on Tommy Carr
picks.blurb: ESPN analysts predict Michigan-Indiana, weigh in on Tommy Carr - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff WNBA Finals: Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview Champions League results Week 7 Fantasy Football Rankings ESPN analysts predict Michigan-Indiana, weigh in on Tommy Carr Isaiah Hole, Wolverines Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 9:50 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's going to be interesting this weekend when Michigan football hosts Indiana, given that the offense came alive with the quarterback switch from Bryce Underwood to Tommy Carr in the second half vs. Penn State . Given that the defense has been solid, if not elite (the Wolverines have the top-rated defense in yards per play), it should keep the game interesting, but if the offense can suddenly move? That could be a game-changer. On the ESPN College GameDay podcast on Wednesday, Dan Wetzel discussed the change, and noted that, in the wide-open Big Ten, the Wolverines aren't exactly out of it. "Michigan team that looked totally dead in the water until halftime of last week and may still be," Wetzel said. "But if Tommy Carr came in, they moved the offense -- he's still a true freshman, I'm not expecting a ton out of this, I don't expect this to happen. But if that sparks it -- there's no doubt that Michigan's got a defense, they've got some running backs. They could get this thing going and be at least a tough team to beat. Can spring some upsets, if not still -- conceivably, I mean, it's on the table and get to 10-2. So there's all sorts of different possibilities. And the Big Ten can make a really interesting race just in that league." That said, Wetzel does believe that the maize and blue will get their third loss this week with the Hoosiers coming to town. But, he does think that the game will be a bit closer than people would have thought just a few short weeks ago. "I'm intrigued as anything about what Michigan does at quarterback," Wetzel said. "Will both guys play: Underwood and Carr? Will they play both at the same time? You know, Utah, I said, Utah runs a two-quarterback system. That's where Whittingham came from. There was a definite spark and some competency and, like, reading run options and RPOs and different things, coming into a game and then starting a game or two different things. There's Whittingham trying to be coy about who's going to start. "How does Underwood respond to all of this? He was a very good teammate on the sideline. Does he come back if he gets back in the game and make some plays? So I'm very interested in what Michigan does. And I think they haven't been interesting all year because they haven't been able to do anything offensively, but I think they're interesting. "I think this is the worst possible opponent they could be playing is Indiana. They need a couple of turnovers. They need some penalties. They need a returned kick a bunch and keep this game low scoring to make it work. And I don't think Indiana is going to give them that. So I'll take the Hoosiers, but fascinating game for the Wolverines, no matter how the result ends up." Rece Davis agrees on all counts. But he thinks this could be a game where the maize and blue find at least some semblance of identity, but can't quite get over the hump of beating the defending national champion. "It's a great opportunity for Michigan, for sure," Davis said. "A great opportunity for Kyle Whittingham to sort of reestablish some confidence in the fan base, but the spot is wrong. away.headline: Ohio State survived Indiana, but Julian Sayin's injury may decide the Buckeyes' season
away.blurb: But that stride was debilitating. Marsh's left foot came down out of bounds, and he knew it immediately. The look on his face was heartbreaking. That misery wasn't felt on the Ohio State sideline. Instead, it was relief, but with questions about what's to come. The primary reason Indiana had a chance to win the game late was that Ohio State's starting QB Julian Sayin was knocked out of the game with an apparent right arm injury earlier in the fourth quarter. Ohio State coach Ryan Day said after the game, without going into specifics about the injury, that Sayin would be out "several weeks." The good news is Ohio State is off next week. The bad news is that when the Buckeyes return from their respite, they'll be on the road to face USC , and then it's a home game with Oregon . While both those teams have had their issues in 2026, the prospect of having to face both with a true freshman at QB is not one that should excite anybody in Scarlet and Gray. If Sayin is out even longer, there are games left against a Northwestern team that's now 5-1 after beating Michigan State , as well as a road game against the Nebraska team that gave Indiana fits last week. Oh, and there's Michigan too. College football can be a brutal sport. Sometimes victory can be taken from you by a toe or two; other times, it comes at a serious cost. That was the case Saturday in Ohio State's 19-15 win over Indiana , a game neither team escaped feeling whole. Indiana's 22-game win streak came to an end in an extremely painful manner. Down five late, on a fourth-and-4 at the Ohio State 27, Indiana opted to go for the throat instead of the first down. Josh Hoover dropped back, found a wide-open Nick Marsh down the sideline, and hit him in stride. After taking a vicious hit from Indiana's Mario Landino, Sayin was seen running to the Ohio State locker room, right arm hanging by his side. He emerged a few minutes later with it in a sling, as the diminutive true freshman Luke Fahey filled in for him, and the Buckeyes offense ground to a complete halt. The Buckeyes didn't manage a first down with Fahey in the game, so while they survived the trip to Bloomington, got revenge on the Hoosiers for last season's Big Ten Championship, and avoided a perilous second loss, there are suddenly concerning questions lingering around the program. While Buckeyes fans everywhere celebrate this win, they'll do so while awaiting an injury report that could determine the fate of their season.

away.headline: Indiana quarterback in discomfort after leaving Ohio State game, returning. What we know
away.blurb: Upon his return, Hoover's performance was mixed, leading to a missed field goal attempt. Hoover previously scrambled for an 8-yard gain but appeared to land on his right elbow. He laid on the turf while trying to shake out his throwing arm, and was attended to by medical staff. IU chose not to take a timeout, causing him to miss a play. An official status update on Hoover was not immediately available. Hoover missed only one play before returning to the game after testing his arm on the sideline. BLOOMINGTON — Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover was wincing in pain after returning from an apparent arm injury and trying to pass against Ohio State on Saturday. As backup Grant Wilson came in to hand off to Lee Beebe Jr., Hoover was seen throwing along the sideline and zipping short throws. He showed he was ready to go in and missed just the one play. Hoover then completed a 16-yard pass to Tyler Morris. Then on third-and-6, he threw a ball to the empty sideline as receiver Nick Marsh ran a seam route. It caused IU to settle for a 55-yard field goal attempt that Nico Radicic missed short. The Hoosiers entered the fourth quarter trailing 13-7. Hoover was sitting alongside the IU offense along the sideline with the defense on the field. He then got up and was throwing along the sideline with Wilson. Hoover was 12 for 24 for 170 yards and had 3 yards on as many rushes (an 11-yard loss for a sack included) entering the fourth quarter.

home.headline: Michigan injury updates: Rod Moore ‘OK’ after being carted off in win
home.blurb: The Wolverines were down a second starting offensive lineman, guard Brady Norton, while center Jake Guarnera and guard Nathan Efobi both played through injuries in Saturday’s 21-18 victory at Michigan Stadium . Guarnera especially, having been listed as a game-time decision two hours before kickoff. “Everyone has something going on at this point in the season,” starting tackle Blake Frazier said. “I’m super proud of him. He was straining all week to make sure that he was giving himself the best opportunity to be out there with us today.” ANN ARBOR, Mich. — Michigan football continues to limp its way through the schedule, and the win over Penn State was no different. Michigan (4-2, 1-2 Big Ten) started backup Avery Gach at right guard while welcoming sixth offensive lineman Manuel Beigel back to the lineup. The Wolverines were able to run for a season-high 211 yards and three touchdowns, much of that coming in the second half with backup Tommy Carr at quarterback. In-game, though, the Wolverines had to deal with a couple of scares. Safety Rod Moore had to be carted off the field in the third quarter after intercepting a Rocco Becht pass; his first turnover of the season. “Should be OK,” Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham said. “It’s nothing major. Now, will he be ready for the next game? That’s debatable, but it’s nothing that’s long term.” That’s good news for Moore, who returned in full this season following a two-year rehab from a torn ACL and meniscus in his knee. He’s started all six games this season and is one of two captains on defense. Meanwhile, cornerback Jyaire Hill was missing in the secondary toward the end of the game, and Whittingham suggested an injury kept him from playing. “But it doesn’t appear to be anything — kind of like Rod — long term,” Whittingham said. Hill struggled in coverage against Penn State receiver Chase Sowell, who caught 11 passes for 151 yards and a touchdown and drew a pair of holding penalties against the senior defensive back. “That receiver is a good receiver,” Whittingham said. “A big, physical kid. I thought we were a little soft in pass defense this game. We needed to get up and challenge a little more, get in the receiver’s face and be a little bit more aggressive in that respect.” To illustrate how beaten up Michigan is, Whittingham said as many as six starters would have been sidelined last week had the Wolverines played a game. They were on a bye instead, giving the team enough time to get some players back in time. “It was good to get those guys healthy and be able to get them to this game and perform,” Whittingham said. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. away.blurb: LSU doesn’t list one of its stars in SEC availability report, signaling a possible return By JON BLAU | Staff writer Jon Blau LSU tight end Trey’Dez Green might be ready for a return this weekend. The Tigers’ preseason All-American was not listed on the Southeastern Conference’s initial availability report for the Auburn game, which is the first time Green hasn’t been listed as “out” since he was sidelined by a knee injury in a loss at Ole Miss in Week 3. LSU’s two other starters sidelined by long-term injuries, linebacker Whit Weeks and safety Dashawn Spears, were still listed as “out” Wednesday for the 11 a.m. Saturday kickoff. It was long believed Green could return after the open date next weekend, allowing him to play in a pivotal home game against Alabama on Nov. 7. But as LSU coach Lane Kiffin said on Oct. 5 before a trip to Kentucky, “If there's anybody that's going to come back sooner than maybe what people thought, it would be him.” Green was out of a knee brace at that time, and Kiffin said he was “getting closer.” Having him back to face Auburn is fortuitous, given the other Tigers just beat then-No. 1 Georgia on Saturday. LSU did list freshman defensive tackle Richard Anderson as doubtful Wednesday for the road trip to Auburn. Reserve linebacker Tylen Singleton, who missed last weekend’s game against Mississippi State, was not listed and should be available. Kiffin said postgame Saturday that doctors held out both Umanmielen and receiver Jackson Harris, who appeared to injure his ankle on a second-half catch. Kiffin didn’t specify their injuries, but he said Sunday he believed Harris would be “fine.” “I feel like if the game went differently, I could have went back out there and played,” Harris told reporters. “So we'll be all good for this week.” Your browser is out of date and potentially vulnerable to security risks. Staff photo by Michael Johnson Meanwhile, Princewill Umanmielen , who is second in the SEC in sacks with 8.5, wasn’t listed in Wednesday’s availability report, either. Umanmielen exited LSU’s win over Mississippi State in the first quarter after a tackle. Green, the 6-foot-7, 237-pound junior, was having a breakout season before he took an Ole Miss helmet to the knee late in a 32-24 loss to the Rebels. He had 14 catches for 222 yards and a touchdown in three games. Harris, who has emerged as LSU’s leading receiver, confirmed as much Tuesday. home.headline: Georgia football injury report: Another starter ruled out for Auburn
home.blurb: Starting Georgia safety KJ Bolden is officially out for Saturday’s clash with Auburn in the Deep South’s Oldest Rivalry. In Friday’s SEC Availability Report , the Bulldogs downgraded Bolden from doubtful to out. Georgia ruled out junior wideout Isiah Canion , sophomore wideout Thomas Blackshear , junior running back Chauncey Bowens , junior EDGE Amaris Williams and freshman defensive back Tyriq Green on Wednesday with the first report of the week. With Canion out, Blackshear had taken on a bigger role, that was until he suffered a collarbone injury in the Vanderbilt game. The Savannah native caught three passes for 33 yards before leaving the game. Blackshear started his first game in Week 4 vs. Oklahoma. Green should be nearing a return after suffering a high-ankle sprain in Week 2. Green suffered the injury shortly after returning a 93-yard kickoff for a touchdown. He underwent tightrope surgery, but Georgia has no need to rush him back. Green was the Bulldogs’ top kick returner through the first two games. After suffering a torn ACL in spring drills, Williams is likely out for the entire regular season. However, he could return for the postseason. Bowens had Lisfranc surgery and is likely done for the rest of the season. He sustained that injury in Georgia’s win over Vanderbilt in Week 5. Bolden came off the field slowly late in Georgia’s win over Alabama after tallying 7 tackles (3 solo), a half tackle for loss and a half sack. After the game, he was wearing a heavy wrap around his left calf muscle. Bolden’s streak of 34 straight games played to start his Georgia career is in jeopardy. He has started 19 of the last 20, missing one first half due to a targeting penalty in the previous game. Frazier, who hasn’t played since Week 3 against Arkansas, is not listed at all. Bolden is a new addition, but he’s battling a lower-body injury. Canion is in line to miss his fourth straight game with a bone bruise in his knee. He traveled to Arkansas last month as Georgia opened SEC play and got the start. He left that game in the opening series after aggravating the injury. The former Georgia Tech standout hasn’t played since. The Bulldogs and Tigers tee it up at 3:30 p.m. ET on ESPN. Georgia will enjoy its only bye of the season in Week 8.

home.headline: Georgia football’s Gunner Stockton injury update after concussion scare vs. Auburn
home.blurb: Further helping things out is that Georgia is headed for a bye week, as the team certainly looked like it could use some time off as it fell apart down the stretch against Auburn. The Georgia football program is currently scrambling for answers following its puzzling loss at home to the unranked Auburn Tigers on Saturday. Gunner Stockton turned in arguably his worst performance as the team’s starter in this one, throwing multiple interceptions and committing a costly fumble late, just as Georgia was driving to try to win the game. Earlier in the game, Stockton had exited briefly after taking a blow to the head, and now, the team has gotten the latest update on his status moving forward. “Georgia QB Gunner Stockton said to be showing no concussion symptoms after Auburn loss,” reported Marc Weiszer of the Athens Banner-Herald on X, formerly Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Some fans joked in poor taste that Stockton seemed to be showing concussion symptoms during the game itself on Saturday, tossing several wildly inaccurate throws and overall looking like a shell of his usual self against an upset-minded Tigers team. The good news for the Bulldogs was that several teams around them in the rankings also fell on Saturday in upset fashion, meaning that Georgia only dropped to number five in this week’s AP Poll, not that Kirby Smart is likely to be putting too much stock into that at this point in the season. However, they’ll have to regroup in time to face the Florida Gators on Halloween, a team that pulled off an upset of its own on Saturday against the Texas Longhorns. Kickoff for that game is set for 3:30 pm ET. Like ClutchPoints’ content? Be sure to follow us. picks.headline: Can Tennessee football avoid letdown at South Carolina, other SEC picks | Adams
picks.blurb: Can Tennessee football avoid letdown at South Carolina, other SEC picks | Adams - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff WNBA Finals: Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview Champions League results Week 7 Fantasy Football Rankings Can Tennessee football avoid letdown at South Carolina, other SEC picks | Adams John Adams, Knoxville News Sentinel Wed, October 21, 2026 at 9:06 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Georgia's Kirby Smart has won so much for so long that he's regarded as the best coach in college football . But after a last-second loss to Auburn, he proved he can also be one of the sport's best quotes. "Humility is a week away," he said. Tennessee coach Josh Heupel would be wise to paraphrase Smart's comment before the Vols take on South Carolina at Williams-Brice Stadium in Columbia. The Vols are coming off a dominant 26-10 victory over Alabama . They're 6-1 and on the cusp of the top 10. But all they gained from a victory over their archrival could be lost with a loss to the unranked Gamecocks. Tennessee 26, South Carolina 16: In an unpredictable SEC season, team performances have varied drastically from one Saturday to the next. Based on that trend, Tennessee could be next in line to take a tumble after a big win. But amid all the SEC's inconsistency, UT's defense has remained steadfast. Something else to consider: Tennessee has been coming on strong in the second half; in South Carolina's last five SEC games dating back to last season, it has lost leads of 27, 16 and 17 points. LSU 31, Auburn 23: While I believe Tennessee's defense will prevent a letdown against South Carolina, I'm not as confident about Auburn's chances for prosperity after upsetting No. 1 Georgia. The LSU offense hasn't always been the model of consistency, but neither has Auburn's. LSU's challenge: Winning on the road. It already has lost at Ole Miss and Kentucky. That's a carryover from the Brian Kelly era. The Tigers lost all four of their SEC road games in 2025. They also lost their last two conference road games in 2024. So, they will take an eight-game SEC road losing streak with them to Jordan-Hare Stadium. They're due. Alabama 30, Texas A&M 15: The Tide also are due for a win after losing back-to-back games against Georgia and Tennessee. They can be grateful that their schedule offers a home game against the three-loss Aggies, who have lost two SEC games by 21 or more points. Texas A&M's 41-0 victory over The Citadel hardly qualifies as the beginning of a turnaround. However, it at least demonstrated that the Aggies aren't devoid of young talent. Freshman running back KJ Edwards led Texas A&M with 116 yards rushing on 16 carries. Freshman wide receiver Aaron Gregory led the Aggies' injury-depleted receiving corps with six catches for 94 yards. Oklahoma 23, Mississippi State 20: This matchup is all about quarterbacks. You can't be sure if Bulldogs quarterback Kamario Taylor is healthy enough to play. Without him, Mississippi State lost 31-0 to LSU. With him, it scored 38 points against Minnesota and 41 on South Carolina. The health of Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer isn't an issue. Performance is his problem. Mateer is a fiery competitor and a running threat. But he doesn't protect the football. He has lost two fumbles and thrown seven interceptions in six games. And he has thrown only two more touchdown passes than interceptions. In Mateer's last season at Washington State (2024), he threw seven interceptions in 12 games. He also threw 29 touchdown passes. Texas 30, Ole Miss 27: The Longhorns are getting less for their NIL money than any other program. But just because you have a big-bucks payroll doesn't mean you have a big-play offense. Texas has scored fewer than 24 points in four of its six games. ADAMS: Tennessee football should be well aware of South Carolina threat on road And the Longhorns are on the verge of playing themselves out of the playoffs for a second consecutive season. But they might be catching the Rebels at the right time. A week after beating LSU, Ole Miss lost to Florida by 28 points. Now, it's coming off a 28-point victory over Missouri. Kentucky 34, Vanderbilt 23: You might conclude that after five consecutive victories, the Wildcats are about to learn, as Smart said, that "humility is a week away." As accurate as Smart's assessment might be in general, it doesn't apply if you're playing Vanderbilt. Record: 59-14 (.793), 48-26 (.642) against the spread. John Adams is a senior columnist. Tennessee is facing one of its scariest tests of the season this weekend. After dominating Alabama last weekend in Knoxville, the Vols are set to head to Columbia this weekend for a matchup against South Carolina. It's a classic trap game for Tennessee in a stadium that's been a house of horrors for the program over the last two decades (the Vols are just 2-6 in Columbia since 2008, and one of those wins came in 2020 when fan attendance was limited due to Covid). South Carolina is coming off a bye week after a big road win against Florida earlier this month. ESPN's Greg McElroy picks winner of Tennessee vs South Carolina ESPN's Greg McElroy, who called the Vols' win over Alabama last weekend, thinks Tennessee will falter in Columbia on Saturday. McElroy has South Carolina beating Tennessee 27-24. “Can South Carolina stop the run that keeps Tennessee on schedule?” said McElroy. “Tennessee has 46 runs of 10 or more yards. That's top nine in the country, and Josh Heupel's teams are 71-9 when they run for 150 yards or more. Look, South Carolina is pretty stingy on those runs. So this is strength against strength, and the pick kind of tilts on whether Tennessee's quarterback can hold up his end of the bargain. “I'm going to take South Carolina to win this game 27-24. I think they're going to win on the ground. They're also coming off a bye. Tennessee just went to war last week against Alabama. They looked amazing doing it, but we've seen teams elevate and then come back to earth the following week, and I think that could happen for Tennessee right here. Because (Matt) Fuller and (LaNorris) Sellers are going to get yards when that first defender misses. Tennessee's linebackers cannot afford to miss in this game. So that (Fuller and Sellers) will keep the Gamecocks out of third and long — which is where Tennessee's sacks live. It shrinks those pass rushing opportunities that are Tennessee's very best weapon.” “Tennessee's defense is amazing,” added McElroy. “They're sixth in points per drive. They're gonna make this thing super tight. But I just lean towards the Gamecocks in this game and the potential flat spot for the Volunteers — even though they bring the better defense into the matchup. The Gamecocks bring a run game and receivers that can win one-on-one. So we will take the Gamecocks.” Vols fans won't love that pick, but it's hard to blame McElroy, who has been pretty accurate with his predictions this season, based on Tennessee's past history in Columbia. This article originally appeared on Topeka Capital-Journal: Kansas State QB Avery Johnson listed as questionable for Arizona State MANHATTAN — Kansas State quarterback Avery Johnson was listed on the Wildcats' injury report Wednesday, Oct. 21, ahead of the team's trip to Arizona State this weekend. Kansas State football coach Collin Klein did not address, and was not asked about, any injury concerns regarding his quarterback during his weekly radio show earlier in the evening. Why is Avery Johnson on the availability report? Though it's unclear what Johnson is dealing with, he notably left the Wildcats' Oct. 17 win over Kansas for one play. After a 59-yard run in the first quarter, Johnson fell awkwardly to the turf and was slow to get up. He was pulled up by both arms, and he walked to the sideline where he smiled and joked with teammates. After missing one play, he returned to the huddle and played the rest of the game with no noticeable injury. He finished 14 of 24 for 209 yards and a touchdown and rushed for 132 yards. Johnson, a third-year starter, has never missed a game due to injury during his Kansas State career. Kansas State will release updates to its availability report Thursday and Friday night, and again 90 minutes before Saturday's kickoff. Who is Kansas State's backup quarterback? Backup Jacob Knuth replaced Johnson for the one play against Kansas, handing the ball to Rodney Fields for a four-yard touchdown. Knuth is a fifth-year player who entered this season having appeared in four games across three seasons in Manhattan. This year, he's played snaps against Nicholls, Washington State and Kansas, completing one pass for seven yards, along with three rushes for 25 yards and a score. Kansas State has dealt with backup quarterback injuries throughout this season. Barnett has been on crutches since the Wildcats' Week 1 win over Nicholls. Sophomore Dillon Duff has appeared on the injury report each week since the Wildcats' Sept. 26 loss at Cincinnati and didn't dress for the first three games. Wyatt D. away.blurb: The Wildcats are in desperate need of someone to step in for Oakley. He was the leading receiver at the position for K-State a year ago. This season, he is among the top players on the roster with NFL interest. During training camp, Klein said he hosted several NFL scouts who were on campus to check out Oakley. Here's Latest Injury Update On Kansas State Wildcats TE Garrett Oakley - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAB Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut Week 7 Fantasy Football Rankings Here's Latest Injury Update On Kansas State Wildcats TE Garrett Oakley (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect) Shandel Richardson Tue, October 20, 2026 at 3:50 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Kansas State Wildcats are expected to once again be without one of their key offensive players this weekend on the road against the Arizona State Sun Devils. K-State coach Collin Klein hinted that tight end Garrett Oakley could miss the third game of the Big 12 conference schedule. Oakley did not play in last week's game against the Kansas Jayhawks in the Sunflower Showdown at Bill Snyder Family Stadium. Here's what Klein had to say during his weekly press conference about the Oakley situation. "Probably unlikely, but we'll see," Klein said. "Day to day." Oakley missed the game because of an undisclosed illness. It gave more opportunities to sophomore Linkon Cure, who is among the most hyped players in program history. He is the first five-star recruit to ever play at Kansas State. While he has gotten off to a slow start, the Wildcats are hoping he can live up to the huge expectations. He has seven catches for 66 yards this season. Last week he caught two passes for 16 yards. The Wildcats need production from Cure because Oakley isn't the only tight end missing. Two weeks ago, it was announced that backup Will Anciaux would miss the season after sustaining a lower leg injury. Klein is also experimenting with moving left tackle Oliver Miller to tight end. That's where he played last week in the win against the Jayhawks. It is unknown if the move is permanent but that's where Miller will play this week. This was a move that was in the works because the Wildcats coaching staff was using him at tight end the past few weeks. A 6-foot-6 freshman, Miller has embraced the opportunity. He was a standout at Cherry Creek (Colo.) High School, where he was rated the No. 41 tackle in the country. Perhaps this could be a better calling for him because of his athleticism. The hope is Oakley is back in uniform sooner than later. He is a big component of the offense and is needed if the Wildcats are going to remain in the hunt for the Big 12 conference championship and College Football Playoff.

picks.headline: ESPN predicts the winner of Clemson football vs. Virginia Tech
picks.blurb: Virginia Tech's Ethan Grunkemeyer leads the Hokies into Memorial Stadium, less than a year after he squared off against the Tigers in the Pinstripe Bowl at Yankee Stadium while playing for Penn State. In that game, Grunkemeyer threw for 260 yards and two touchdowns in Penn State's 22-10 win over Clemson. A third-year QB who committed to the Nittany Lions and James Franklin, Grunkemeyer followed his former Penn State coach to Blacksburg after Franklin was hired by Virginia Tech last November after the Nittany Lions parted ways with the 12-year skipper barely a month earlier. He has thrown for 1,984 yards and 15 touchdowns to two interceptions through seven games this season. Grunkemeyer and Virginia Tech lead the ACC in passing yards , though the Hokies have played one more game than Darian Mensah and the No. 1-ranked Miami Hurricanes. Clemson's passing game has been a complete contrast, to say the least. Through their first six contests, the Tigers have thrown a combined two touchdown psases between Week 1 starter Christopher Vizzina and former four-star freshman Tait Reynolds. The Tigers are second to last in the ACC in total offense with 340.7 yards per game while Virginia Tech ranks sixth (449.7) in the conference. Reynolds was 17 of 26 for 127 yards in Clemson's 37-0 win over Charleston Southern in Week 6. He has thrown for 943 yards with one touchdown and three interceptions entering his fifth start of 2026. Will Clemson football beat Virginia Tech? ESPN's prediction Oddsmakers have Clemson as a 2.5-point favorite over Virginia Tech, but as always, ESPN Analytics has its own odds for Saturday's game. ESPN's matchup predictor , which offers a prediction model based on its college football power index and other variables, gives Clemson a 55.9% chance to win. Virginia Tech has a 44.1% chance. The Tigers are No. 48 in ESPN's FPI with a 6.5 rating, which ranks 10th among ACC teams. Virginia Tech has a 6.6 rating that's one spot ahead of Clemson in ESPN's metrics. The Tigers are one spot ahead of Oregon State (6.0) in the FPI. Clemson football has longshot odds of reaching ACC title game entering Week 8 In ESPN's FPI entering Week 8, Clemson's chances of reaching six wins to qualify for a bowl game stand at 88.4%. The Tigers' chances of winning the ACC, however, are just 0.3%. That's down from 0.9% before the Tigers' 41-13 loss to the Miami Hurricanes on Oct. 3. Clemson's chances of reaching the 12-team College Football Playoff are 1.5%, which is down from 4.1% prior to the Miami loss and down from 22.2% entering the season. Ratings and projections update daily. FPI data from seasons prior to 2019 may not be complete." away.blurb: BLACKSBURG — Following a win over Georgia Tech, Virginia Tech football heads out on the road to face Clemson in a pivotal ACC game. Ahead of the clash, the ACC revealed the initial player availability report for both teams this week. The player availability report, which was first used for the 2025 season, provides five types of designations prior to game day: available, probable, questionable, doubtful, and out. A player being available means that they are not designated on the list. Eleven players are on this week's report for Virginia Tech, the same as Week 6 against Cal and Week 7 against Georgia Tech. Here's how the availability report shakes out by position: The Hokies' loss against Pitt came in spite of them racing out to an early 14-0 lead. The Panthers roared back with a 35-10 response, leading by as many as 11 in the final quarter. Though the Hokies mounted a nine-point rally, fifth-year kicker John Love's 36-yard game-deciding field goal was ruled no good. Initial Availability Report Released for Virginia Tech-Georgia Tech: Who's In, Out, TBD For Hokies? Here's the list of players posted on the initial availability report, organized by status: Offensive Line: 4 (Terry, Wright, Austin, Cunningham) Wide Receiver: 3 (Peterkin, Booker, Stuewe) Cornerback: 2 (Williams, Chadwick) Following its first 4-0 start since the 2017 season with wins over VMI , Old Dominion , Maryland , and Boston College , Virginia Tech (5-2, 2-2 ACC) lost back-to-back clashes with Pitt and Cal. Both were by one score, marking the first time since September 2024 that the Hokies have lost back-to-back games by seven points or fewer. The following week, Virginia Tech lost to Cal 25-20 in Berkeley. The Hokies held a 14-13 lead entering the final quarter, allowing the Golden Bears to pull ahead. Virginia Tech scored a go-ahead touchdown with 1:15 to go, but Cal's six-play, 75-yard drive — aided by a pair of penalty calls for roughing the passer (Kaleb Spencer) and defensive pass interference (Kenny Woseley Jr.) — enabled it to score the game-winning touchdown with 18 seconds remaining. Virginia Tech marched the ball down to Cal's 7-yard line with three seconds remaining, but quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer's last-gasp throw to a contested Luke Reynolds was incomplete. The Hokies bounced back last week, though, with a 34-24 victory over Georgia Tech in Lane Stadium. Virginia Tech held a 24-3 lead at intermission and despite being outscored by 11 in the second half, it held firm. Grunkemeyer threw for 215 yards in the first half, though he only logged 35 more passing yards over the final two quarters. This year, Grunkemeyer's completed 72.9% of his passes for 1,984 yards (No. 4 in FBS), 15 touchdowns and two interceptions. There will be four reports in total: today's report, one report on Thursday and Friday, plus a game-day report two hours before Virginia Tech's tussle with Clemson. away.headline: Clemson football vs Virginia Tech injury report includes one Hokies starter
away.blurb: Starting Virginia Tech cornerback Thomas Williams is listed as questionable on the initial injury report for Clemson football's Week 8 ACC game against the Hokies . The initial report was released on Oct. 21. Cam Chadwick Jr., listed as a backup cornerback on the Hokies' depth chart, is also on the injury report as probable. On Clemson 's end, wide receiver Gordon Sellars III is listed as out. Tigers coach Dabo Swinney said that Sellars has a concussion and is going through concussion protocol. He's made three catches for 8 yards in a backup role. Defensive tackle Devarrick Woods and running back Jarvis Green don't appear on the injury report for Clemson. Swinney has said that he expects both players to return from injury against Virginia Tech. Vizzina was removed from the Tigers' injury report against California on Sept. 25 ahead of kickoff that night and hasn't appeared once since. However, Vizzina hasn't fully recovered, and he was only available for emergencies against Miami and Charleston Southern. WR Shamarius Peterkin (questionable) CB Thomas Williams (questionable) OL Nathaniel Wright (questionable) OL Montavious Cunningham (questionable) The Tigers (4-2, 2-1 ACC) square off with Virginia Tech (5-2, 2-2) at home on Oct. 24 (7 p.m., ESPN). Williams, a Greenville native, has recorded eight total tackles, two forced fumbles, one interception and one pass defended this season. He's started three games and was listed as a starter on Virginia Tech's official depth chart this week. Start the day smarter. Get all the news you need in your inbox each morning. Christopher Vizzina injury update Swinney said backup quarterback Christopher Vizzina is having his "best week by far" of the season and that he's 90% healthy. Vizzina has been recovering from a small fracture in his left elbow after originally injuring it against Georgia Southern on Sept. 12. Swinney said after the Charleston Southern game that he wouldn't have had an issue with playing Vizzina against the Buccaneers, but that Vizzina told him he wasn't ready and that Brock Bradley should enter instead. Trent Pearman and Bradley entered, respectively, after Clemson pulled starter Tait Reynolds with the game well in hand. "I asked him. I said, 'Do you want to go in, or do you want to put Brock in?' And he's like, 'Let's put Brock in,'" Swinney said. "So that was really his call. Coach C.V." home.headline: Clemson football vs Virginia Tech injury report includes one Hokies starter
home.blurb: Starting Virginia Tech cornerback Thomas Williams is listed as questionable on the initial injury report for Clemson football's Week 8 ACC game against the Hokies . The initial report was released on Oct. 21. Cam Chadwick Jr., listed as a backup cornerback on the Hokies' depth chart, is also on the injury report as probable. On Clemson 's end, wide receiver Gordon Sellars III is listed as out. Tigers coach Dabo Swinney said that Sellars has a concussion and is going through concussion protocol. He's made three catches for 8 yards in a backup role. Defensive tackle Devarrick Woods and running back Jarvis Green don't appear on the injury report for Clemson. Swinney has said that he expects both players to return from injury against Virginia Tech. Vizzina was removed from the Tigers' injury report against California on Sept. 25 ahead of kickoff that night and hasn't appeared once since. However, Vizzina hasn't fully recovered, and he was only available for emergencies against Miami and Charleston Southern. WR Shamarius Peterkin (questionable) CB Thomas Williams (questionable) OL Nathaniel Wright (questionable) OL Montavious Cunningham (questionable) The Tigers (4-2, 2-1 ACC) square off with Virginia Tech (5-2, 2-2) at home on Oct. 24 (7 p.m., ESPN). Williams, a Greenville native, has recorded eight total tackles, two forced fumbles, one interception and one pass defended this season. He's started three games and was listed as a starter on Virginia Tech's official depth chart this week. Start the day smarter. Get all the news you need in your inbox each morning. Christopher Vizzina injury update Swinney said backup quarterback Christopher Vizzina is having his "best week by far" of the season and that he's 90% healthy. Vizzina has been recovering from a small fracture in his left elbow after originally injuring it against Georgia Southern on Sept. 12. Swinney said after the Charleston Southern game that he wouldn't have had an issue with playing Vizzina against the Buccaneers, but that Vizzina told him he wasn't ready and that Brock Bradley should enter instead. Trent Pearman and Bradley entered, respectively, after Clemson pulled starter Tait Reynolds with the game well in hand. "I asked him. I said, 'Do you want to go in, or do you want to put Brock in?' And he's like, 'Let's put Brock in,'" Swinney said. "So that was really his call. Coach C.V." Dabo talks Clemson’s shutout win vs. Charleston Southern, updates injuries
home.blurb: “I’ve been around here a minute, and we’ve had some games like this over the years where I’m not real happy in the fourth quarter because we’re sloppy. You’re playing a bunch of guys (backups), and all of a sudden you lose your edge a little bit. I felt they never lost their edge. They played tough. It’s hard to shut people out.” “It’s hard to shut people out. They had three yards in the second half, and we played 90 guys or more, so played a lot of guys. I thought they (the backups) just kept showing up.” “We’re a work in progress. ... Devarrick Woods (who didn’t dress Saturday due to injury) is gonna help us. ... Kourtney Kelly was so happy to be out there again, and I think Vic Burley had his best game. He played stout.” “I’d just come out of the tunnel to go to the bus, and I saw those F-16s (flyover planes) coming. You don’t hear them until they’re past you, which is probably bad news for the enemy, right?” No sweat: Clemson football shuts out Charleston Southern. Key ACC stretch looms Here are quick hits from coach Dabo Swinney’s postgame news conference: “Proud of the team. We handled our business, and good to get the win. Fun to see us play well. Fun to see us execute probably the best we have collectively.” “We dominated the opponent, and we played complementary football.” “The biggest issue to me is we lost the turnover margin. ... If we wanna have a good finish to our season and in conference play, we’ve gotta clean that up.” On kicker Nolan Hauser’s career long 59-yard make “We called a timeout and I threw up some grass to test the wind and said, ‘Let’s do it.’ I asked him and he said he wanted to try it. ... He needed 50 yards and he kicked it 59 yards and one inch. ... He’s kicking with confidence.” On QB Tait Reynolds, passing offense struggles “I thought Tait played his best game. ... You’ve gotta catch the ball. The drops were the most frustrating thing. He ( Reynolds ) put some balls right on the money.” “If we catch a few of those touchdowns, you’re probably not asking me that. We’ve gotta finish.” “He (Reynolds) threw three to T.J. (Moore) who were right on the money. He threw one to (Bryant) Wesco that was right on the money. Those guys are great players. It wasn’t a great day for T.J. today, but he’ll bounce back.” On Reynolds leaving the game for one play in third quarter “He was a little mad at me, but he was gimpy. ... he goes, ‘I’m going back in next play.’ I said, ‘No, you’re not. You’ll go back in when I put you in. ... It was all good, because I didn’t want people to think he was hurt.” “He was just a little banged up, a little gimpy in the moment.” On QB Christopher Vizzina’s injury status “He’s not 100%. ... I actually asked him if he wanted to go in on the last drive and he said, ‘No, put in Brock (Bradley) .’ So he was Coach CV there.” “This was the first week he was really able to practice the way he needs to practice. ... home.headline: Clemson QB Christopher Vizzina takes big step toward injury return
home.blurb: Clemson QB Christopher Vizzina takes big step toward injury return - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Clemson QB Christopher Vizzina takes big step toward injury return That progress includes moving from the larger brace to a sleeve and pad. Vizzina is still working to regain his full range of motion, so Swinney's update stops short of confirming a return to game action. True freshman Tait Reynolds took over as Clemson 's starter ahead of the North Carolina game after Vizzina started the first two contests. Vizzina was completely unavailable against the Tar Heels, then dressed against Cal strictly as an emergency option. Swinney made clear just how limited that availability was. Clemson would have turned to Trent Pearman and likely Brock Bradley before asking Vizzina to play against the Golden Bears. This article originally appeared on Clemson Wire: Clemson QB Christopher Vizzina takes big step toward injury return Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut Week 7 Fantasy Football Rankings Drew Landon, Clemson Wire Thu, October 15, 2026 at 5:33 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Christopher Vizzina has not played since suffering a left elbow injury against Georgia Southern in Week 2. His recovery has taken longer than Clemson initially expected, but head coach Dabo Swinney offered an encouraging update following Wednesday's practice. "CV is still not 100%, but this has been the best week he's had since before he got hurt," Swinney said. "He's just gotten better and better. We thought it would bounce back a little bit quicker, but it's just been hard for him," Swinney said. "But he's gotten better. He's had a really good week, and it's just one of those things that's been day-to-day." "It would have been like we would have had to get through Trent and probably even through Brock before we got to him," Swinney said. "He was just still really, really sore." Through his two starts, Vizzina completed 14 of 23 passes for 102 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. Manning threw for 173 yards, completed 14 of 20 passes, and threw one touchdown. According to former UCLA head coach Rick Neuheisel, Texas will need to make key adjustments to its strategy ahead of the upcoming game. During an appearance on CBS Sports, Neuheisel picked Ole Miss to win. "I'm concerned for Texas in this game, not because I don't think they'll play hard and be geared up to play their best game of the season, but I feel like because of all the pressure on Arch, they're going to condense, and condensing will not be the answer to going against Pete Golding defense," he said . Neuheisel pointed out that Arch Manning attempted just 20 passes against Florida, arguing that such an approach will not be effective against the Ole Miss Rebels. While the Texas Longhorns have won four of their six games this season, Manning has shown only flashes of brilliance rather than the consistency expected of him. Overall, Manning has completed 106 of 166 passes for 1,295 yards, 11 touchdowns, and five interceptions. After his performance against the Gators, speculation began that he could be benched for the upcoming game. However, head coach Steve Sarkisian made it clear that Arch Manning will remain the team's starting quarterback. "There's no doubt about it, Arch can play better for us, but he's our starter," he said , per Fox Sports. "We need to see a better version of him this week." Sarkisian said Manning is a quality player and that, as a coach, it is his job to bring out the best in him on the field. Former Texas Coach Heaps Praise on Arch Manning On an episode of THE STAMPEDE, former Texas coach Mack Brown said Arch Manning and the rest of the Longhorns are playing under immense pressure. He believes the team needs to free itself from that pressure before stepping onto the field. In Brown's view, Manning has the talent and ability to help get Texas back on track. "Arch's gotta go back and be the Arch we saw at the last of last year," he said. "He's good enough, he's athletic enough, he's smart enough, and for a 22-year-old, he has handled this pressure so well." Brown said the upcoming matchup against the Ole Miss Rebels will be crucial for the Longhorns and could shape their chances of making the College Football Playoff this season. By Braden Ramsey Published: Oct 21, 2026 · 1:46 PM EDT There are only two ranked-on-ranked matchups on the Week 8 college football slate. While Houston-Utah will draw plenty of eyeballs, the SEC will be locked in on Ole Miss-Texas in Austin. The Rebels (5-1, 3-1 SEC) have only one ranked foe on their schedule after this battle with the Longhorns. If they can handle business on the road, they will feel very secure in their College Football Playoff positioning. Meanwhile, the Longhorns (4-2, 1-2 SEC) would be all but eliminated from the CFP chase if they suffered a third consecutive defeat. ESPN's Greg McElroy broke down the matchup on his Always College Football program. He believes Ole Miss becomes a real SEC Championship contender with a victory. “If Ole Miss wins, the national narrative is that Ole Miss is a real SEC title contender… they would be 4-1 in the league,” McElroy said. “Here's the detail that makes Ole Miss very dangerous: they don't play Kentucky or Tennessee this year… when Georgia comes to Oxford on Nov. 7, that game is essentially a play-in for Atlanta.” On the other side of the coin, McElroy thinks a Texas loss is something the nation is salivating about. A win, though, would thrust them back into the CFP picture because of their early season triumphs against Ohio State and Tennessee. “For Texas, a loss is the story the whole country has just been waiting to write… [and] the conference title's gone in October,” McElroy claimed. “If Texas wins, the national narrative is, ‘the most dangerous two-loss team in the country just reminded everybody why [they're dangerous]'… you beat Ole Miss… you now have three teams that you've beaten all power rated in the top 12.” Hear more from McElroy here: The Rebels and Longhorns kick off at 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday night (ABC). picks.headline: No. 19 Texas vs. No. 7 Ole Miss opponent preview: Rebels head to Austin for first matchup as conference foes
picks.blurb: No. 19 Texas vs. No. 7 Ole Miss opponent preview: Rebels head to Austin for first matchup as conference foes | Burnt Orange Nation Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Texas Longhorns Community Burnt Orange Nation October 22, 2026 Burnt Orange Nation Notifications Notifications Get The App Sections Texas Longhorns Recruiting Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Texas Football Odds Texas Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search Get The App Sections Expand Texas Longhorns Recruiting Betting Expand Betting News All communities Notifications Texas Longhorns Football A talented Rebels team comes to Austin for a top-25 matchup on Saturday. With a 5-1 record and Top 10 ranking, the No. 7 Ole Miss Rebels head to Austin on Saturday to face off against a struggling Texas Longhorns team that dropped to No. 19 in the AP Top 25 after consecutive losses to unranked opponents. The first matchup between the two foes in 13 years, Saturday’s battle is the first as conference opponents with the Longhorns leading the all time series 6-2. After a deep College Football Playoff run to the semifinals last season also featured controversy with former head coach Lane Kiffin, Ole Miss and first-year head coach Pete Golding are continuing that success — the Rebels already have three ranked wins and have bounced back with consecutive wins after getting beaten by Florida. The Rebels boast one of the most prolific passing attacks in the SEC behind star quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, who is joined by an elite duo in running back Kewan Lacy and wide receiver Deuce Alexander. Defensively, Ole Miss has been inconsistent, giving up 40-plus points in two matchups, but also holding multiple conference opponents to under 20 points. Golding was promoted from the defensive coordinator position, giving his team a clear identity and scheme continuity that isn’t traditional for first-year head coaches. The matchup on Saturday is the biggest road test for the Rebels and yet another litmus test of whether Ole Miss will be a national title contender this year. Here’s how the Rebels stack up position by position. Ole Miss has one of the most experienced and dangerous quarterbacks in the nation in Trinidad Chambliss, who has been electric after taking over the starting role during the middle of last season, currently ranking third in the Heisman Trophy odds at FanDuel. Through six games, he has accumulated 1,676 yards on a 67.6 completion percentage with 14 touchdowns and four interceptions. However, Chambliss does his best work when navigating the pocket. His ability to extend plays and use his legs makes him extremely difficult to defend. You can’t just get pressure on him, you must maintain rush-lane integrity and perhaps even devote a spy to defending him, otherwise he will make plays with his legs. Facing one of the sports biggest stars, the Texas defense has a monumental challenges on Saturday. The priority has to be making the offense one dimensional and maintaining discipline when rushing the passer. Joining Chambliss in the backfield is another star in running back Kewan Lacy. A year ago, Lacy was recognized as an All-American behind his 1,567 rushing yards and 24 touchdowns. Through five games, with one missed due to injury, he has recorded 352 rushing yards and five touchdowns while averaging 5.7 yards per attempt. Lacy has shown to be tough and injury-prone. He missed a game earlier this season thanks to a shoulder injury and was banged up against Missouri with a lower-body issue. However, neither stopped him. Despite missing most of the second quarter last Saturday, he still rushed for a season-high 122 yards on 16 carries. If Lacy can manage to play the full game on Saturday, he is lethal and will be playing with an extra chip on his shoulder. “It’s going to mean a lot, just coming back home,” Lacey said. “It’s a hometown game, so I’m excited to have all my family, friends there.” The Lancaster product was a Texas fan during his childhood and actually wanted to become a Longhorn, but he ended up signing with Missouri after Texas failed to extend an offer in the 2024 recruiting cycle, signing Jerrick Gibson and Christian Clark instead. “I wanted to commit to UT,” Lacy said at SEC Media Days in July. “That was my dream my freshman year, I wanted to go to Texas. But my process throughout my high school career, I never really got an opportunity from them.” Come Saturday, Lacy will have a huge opportunity to showcase what the Longhorns missed out on. If he can’t go, the Rebels will turn to transfer Mekhi Frazier and freshman JT Lindsey to handle the load. Frazier arrived on campus this past season after leading Michigan State in rushing yards last year. He’s recorded 254 yards on 45 carries this season. Wide receiver The leading threat in the pass game is Deuce Alexander, but the Rebels possess a deep and talented wide out room with plenty of players that can help move the ball. Alexander caught 44 passes for 684 yards and two touchdowns last year behind second-round draft pick De’Zhaun Stribling, while adding 122 yards on the ground. This season as WR1, he’s nearly reached that mark halfway through the year with 35 catches for 523 yards and five touchdowns. At 14.9 yards per catch, Alexander is a downfield threat that can generate chunk plays in a hurry. He started his career in the slot but has emerged as a player that can use his speed from any point on the field. His top-end speed is elite and forces the defense to shade over to prevent the deep ball. Behind Alexander are Traylon Ray and Horatio Fields, who have combined for 39 catches and 509 yards this season. Ray is another downfield option while Fields is a more reliable target that can shoulder the load when defenses prioritize Alexander and Ray. Former Longhorn Johntay Cook is also on the roster and has recorded eight catches for 74 yards and a score. Tight end Caleb Odom is another reliable threat for Chambliss. In five games, he’s tallied 21 catches for 267 yards and two touchdowns, which slots him second on the team in receptions. Odom is a drive-extending pass catcher. At 12.7 yards per reception and a season long of 35 yards, he’s not going to decimate a defense down the field, but rather provide Chambliss with an intermediate option. Most importantly, Odom can attack the middle of the field and provide matchup problems when opposing defense are forced to prioritize Alexander or stack the box to stop Lacy. The 6’5, 245-pound junior is in his second season at Ole Miss after appearing in 12 games for Alabama as a freshman in 2024. He’s stepped up dramatically after seeing just a handful of targets last year and has positioned himself as a legitimate threat this season. If you can somehow stop the run, minimize Chambliss’ legs, and cover the wideouts, Odom can decimate you on quick passes and intermediate throws. Offensive line The Ole Miss offensive line comes to Austin riding high after one of the best performances of the season last week. The Rebels ran for 257 yards while averaging 6.7 yards per carry last week, and the front five as a whole graded as the highest unit in the country, according to Pro Football Network. Heading into the year, the offensive line had holes to fill thanks to two NFL departures. A host of transfers were brought in and have done a solid job in six games. Leading the way is right guard Patrick Kutas, while left tackle Terez Davis is another steady presence on the other side of the line. Disrupting the line up front will be key to stopping the run and disrupting Chambliss. If Texas can win up front without needing to stack the box, the Longhorn defense will be in a good spot. As a whole, the offense for Ole Miss can attack a defense in a variety of ways. With elite skill position players that can rack up huge plays and one of the best quarterbacks in the country, the Longhorn defense has their work cut out for them. Winning individual battles will be key on Saturday. With a multi-dimensional offense that can attack you in so many different ways, Muschamp will need to pick and choose who he leaves on an island and hope that they succeed. The defense is headed by Bryan Brown, who is the sole defensive coordinator after sharing the role with Golding before Golding’s promotion. Though Brown is the defensive coordinator, this unit is heavily influenced by Golding, who likes to use a mix of twists and stunts to create pressure and stop the run game up front. This year, the unit has been middle of the pack in conference play. The unit suffocated Missouri and Vanderbilt, but also gave up 52 to Florida. Running the ball has proven most effective against Ole Miss, a part of the game Texas hasn’t looked exceptional at. Here are the key Rebels to keep an eye on. Defensive line Leading the charge up front is defensive tackle Will Echoles, an established disruptor. As a sophomore last season, Echoles was recognized as first-team All-SEC, according to the AP, after registering five sacks, 11.5 tackles for loss, and 68 total tackles. According to Pro Football Focus, he led the Power Four in pressures and defensive stops. When Echoles isn’t getting pressure, he utilizes his hands very well. Last season, he batted down the ninth-most passes among all defensive linemen in college football. This season, he’s already gotten off to a hot start with 18 tackles and 1.5 sacks. He will undoubtedly impact the game so ensuring Echoles doesn’t do so routinely will be key for the Longhorn offense. On the edge, Cam Franklin and Blake Purchase can disrupt plays if not blocked properly. Purchase leads the team with 3.5 sacks while also adding 23 tackles and a forced fumble. He shined against Vanderbilt with a two-sack performance. If the Longhorns can’t keep a clean pocket, the Texas offense will struggle. The Ole Miss front four isn’t the most talented in the conference, but still has more than enough players to attack inside or on the edge. The teeth of the defense is the linebacker room. Led by Suntarine Perkins with heavy contributions from Luke Ferrelli, Keaton Thomas, and Tah’j Butler, this group is the best unit in Golding’s defense. Perkins is a hybrid-style player with great speed and athleticism. He’s good in coverage and can rush the passer. Two years ago he recorded 10.5 sacks for the Rebels. Ferrelli is the leading tackler for the Rebels and has become a great piece for Golding after a controversial offseason in which Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney accused Golding of tampering after Ferrelli committed to the Tigers, but changed his mind and opted to join Golding. Originally at Cal, Ferrelli was the ACC Defensive Rookie of the Year last season and has continued that success with a team leading 39 tackles in addition to two sacks. Thomas has been strong against the run and in tackling but has struggled in pass coverage, something Texas can exploit come Saturday. As a whole, the linebackers have experience, top end talent, and depth making them an important part of the Ole Miss defense. Cornerback Jaylon Braxton and safety Joenel Aguero are the two premier defenders on the back end. Braxton lines up on the outside opposite of Antonio Kite, the other corner for the Rebels. Braxton is an experienced defender and will flash his hat tackling. He’s got 23 tackles and an interception to his name this year. While he will give up catches, he does a good job limited yardage. Meanwhile, Kite brings a veteran presence after starting 12 games for Ole Miss last year. He’s had a solid year, grading at 69.9 in coverage according to Pro Football Focus. Playing free safety, Aguero is a versatile defender in his first season at Ole Miss after spending three season as a Georgia Bulldog in which he appeared in 35 games including starting all 12 last season. away.headline: Texas releases injury report for Ole Miss matchup
away.blurb: Texas star edge Colin Simmons is listed as doubtful for Saturday’s matchup after sustaining a high ankle sprain in the loss to Florida, while running back Hollywood Smothers is listed as questionable. Smothers reportedly missed practice on Monday due to a shoulder injury. Other names listed for the Longhorns are wide receiver Kaliq Lockett and offensive lineman Jaydon Chatman (both questionable), as well as freshman edge Richard Wesley (out). Simmons going down during the Florida game is a huge blow for the Texas defense, as he has been playing at an extremely high level. Texas defensive coordinator Will Muschamp is going to need all hands on deck on Saturday to defend Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, who has been one of the most dynamic playmakers in the country at the quarterback position, especially with the surprise news that Wesley is out. On top of that, Ole Miss will likely have star running back Kewan Lacy back on the field, as he is listed as probable on tonight’s injury report. The initial SEC injury report was released for the Saturday matchup between the No. 19 Texas Longhorns and against the No. 7 Ole Miss Rebels on Wednesday and while the Rebels have many more players on their side of the injury report, there are certainly some notable names for the Longhorns as well. Every game moving forward is a must-win for the Longhorns after dropping the last two matchups. They will need to get healthy moving forward as they try to navigate a difficult stretch in the schedule with eight straight games to close the season.

away.blurb: Texas edge rusher Colin Simmons is listed as doubtful for the upcoming SEC contest at Royal-Memorial Stadium. Simmons exited last week's 27-24 loss to the Florida Gators early in the fourth quarter due to a right-leg injury, and he did not return to the game. Simmons will look to continue his climb up two all-time Texas leaderboards upon his potential return to the field this week/later this season. Simmons raised his career sack total to 31 1/2 in the loss to Florida, moving him to No. 3 on Texas' all-time leaderboard (and nine sacks behind Kiki DeAyala's program-record 40.5 sacks). Simmons also has DeAyala's single-season record in his sights. Simmons exited the weekend with 10 1/2 sacks in 2026, 12 sacks behind DeAyala's record-setting 22 1/2-sack season in 1982. Texas will face perhaps college football's best quarterback Saturday when Ole Miss ' Trinidad Chambliss comes to Austin. The Longhorns (4-2, 1-2 SEC) will likely do so without their best defensive player. Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian said Saturday he believed Simmons suffered a right-knee injury against Florida, but was unaware of the injury's severity. Sarkisian didn't elaborate on Simmons' injury Monday, but Orangeblood's Anwar Richardson reported Simmons will miss three-to-four weeks due to a high-ankle sprain. Simmons' exit against Florida halted his statistical climb and hindered the Longhorns defense. Texas will likely now be without Simmons against Ole Miss and Chambliss, a scary situation after back-to-back SEC losses. Read this story on statesman.com

away.headline: Kewan Lacy's Texas Homecoming Comes With an Injury Question for Ole Miss
away.blurb: "So I think every week is going to be pretty similar with him. I mean, you’ve got an experienced player that’s been in the system, right? So, you know, our responsibility throughout the week is to make sure we’re protecting him and taking care of him," Golding said on Monday. "It’s not like he’s forgot how to play football. So obviously the game plan is going to change a little bit week in and week out...But as far as, you know, the physicality of having to run the football, you know, versus scout team and all that, it’s not that..." For the second straight week, Kewan Lacy returns to familiar grounds. Last week, Lacy finished with 122 rushing yards against his former team, the Missouri Tigers. This week, Lacy returns to his home state of Texas. The Ole Miss running back attended Lancaster High School, located just outside of downtown Dallas. Lacy grew up a Texas Longhorns fan, and he'll have a chance to play against his childhood team, but his availability comes with caution. Keeping Lacy Healthy is a Top Priority Lacy has battled injuries all season. He missed one game with a shoulder injury, but even when Lacy was on the field, Rebels fans hadn't seen the star running back fully unlocked until Saturday. Lacy looked like his 2025 self against the Tigers. Lacy and Ole Miss would love to build on that momentum against Texas. But Pete Golding is remaining cautious with Lacy and his workload throughout the week. Lacy handled 306 carries last season. The Rebels leaned on him more than they'd like, so the coaching staff appears much more cautious with Lacy this season. He'll likely take it easy during practice and he'll be ramped up on gameday. This year, Ole Miss has someone who can take pressure off Lacy. Makhi Frazier is averaging 5.6 yards per carry on 45 attempts. Frazier's running ability makes life easier for Lacy and gives opposing defenses a different look at running back. As mentioned earlier, Lacy returns to the school he grew up watching. During SEC Media Days, Lacy said he wanted to commit to Texas, but the Longhorns never gave him an opportunity. Now, he'll be on the opposing side with his family in the crowd. “It’s going to mean a lot, just coming back home. I don’t really hold anything against Texas," Lacy said. "But it’s a hometown game, so I’m excited to have all my family, friends there.” If the Rebels are going to pull off a massive road victory, they'll need Lacy to have another dominant game. picks.headline: Vanderbilt defense preview: Kentucky offense can dominate
picks.blurb: Vanderbilt defense preview: Kentucky offense can dominate - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff WNBA Finals: Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview Champions League results Week 7 Fantasy Football Rankings Story by Wildcats Wire Vanderbilt defense preview: Kentucky offense can dominate Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 4:14 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football will host Vanderbilt under the lights at Kroger Field on Saturday night, as it is the final game before the Wildcats enter a much needed bye week. The first College Football Playoff rankings will happen in two weeks after the Wildcats bye week, and there is a great chance we see Kentucky on the graphic if they can improve to 7-1 against Vanderbilt. There shouldn't be any extra motivation needed, as a lot of these players remember the beatdown that happened in Nashville last season when Vanderbilt defeated Kentucky 45-17 in a blowout fashion. Kentucky has an opportunity to return the favor on Saturday, as the Commodores have one of the worst defenses in the SEC. Vanderbilt is struggling in a lot of ways on the defensive side of the football, and Kentucky's offense should be able to capitalize. The Commodores rank last in the SEC in pressure rate and tackle for loss rate, they have had a difficult time of forcing negative plays. Vanderbilt also allows the highest success rate in conference, and Kentucky ranks fourth in the SEC in offensive success rate. The real key to watch in my opinion is early down conversion rate and third down conversion rate, Vanderbilt's defense allows the highest percentage to opponents in the SEC; Kentucky's offense is one of the best in the country at converting on early downs and they have a chance to improve on third downs this weekend. There are a few players to watch on Vanderbilt's defense, and we will get more into that when we release our X factors for the game. It starts up front with veteran edge defender Miles Capers and defensive tackle Issa Ouattara who is a massive 6'7, 305-pound lineman that clogs up the middle. On the back end, senior safety CJ Heard is a player who plays in the box and can make plays all over the field; Heard is dangerous as a blitzer, he is a sure tackler and is probably the best player on the team in coverage. However, there is a stark contrast in this defense compared to the one the Wildcats just faced in Oklahoma. Vanderbilt has allowed 121 total points in their last three games against Georgia, Ole Miss and Arkansas. The Commodores are allowing 40 points per game over the last three weeks. This is probably the worst defense left on Kentucky's schedule. This creates a perfect opportunity for the Wildcats to get things going offensively to improve to 7-1 heading into the bye week. Vanderbilt has the lowest pressure and tackle for loss rate in the SEC, as previously mentioned, so this is a game where all eyes are on the Kentucky offensive line. This is a game they should dominate, they can get movement in the running game and keep Minchey clean for 60 minutes. Vanderbilt is allowing over four yards per carry and 146 rushing yards per game. You have to wonder if the coaching staff keeps CJ Baxter out of this game to get him to the bye week so he is as close to 100% as possible for the final stretch; this could be another heavy Jason Patterson and Jovantae Barnes game. Kentucky has yet to put together four quarters of football where they are firing on all cylinders. I think this is the game we could see that play out, specifically from an offensive standpoint. Now that the Wildcats are in the thick of the College Football Playoff hunt, how you win in these games can matter to a degree. Kentucky needs a dominant win on Saturday to keep that momentum going into the bye week.
