Kentucky just played one of the best defenses in the SEC in Oklahoma , and now they get to play one of the worst as we previewed the Vanderbilt defense . On the offensive side of the football, the Commodores are led by five star true freshman quarterback Jared Curtis. The offense has struggled but Curtis has shown plenty of flashes although he has a ton of room to grow. In our Vanderbilt defensive preview, we really centered it around Kentucky's offense and how they can exploit the Commodores defense. We are going to do the same here because this game is about Kentucky staying focused to enter the bye week with a 7-1 record. Jared Curtis has a rocket for an arm and is a big, physical runner. Kentucky head coach Will Stein said that Curtis plays like Josh Allen, but he made it clear he was not making the comparison. Coach Stein is correct though, Curtis can make unreal throws down the field and runs with physicality that is rare at the quarterback position. However, Curtis has a long way to become the dangerous player he is capable of. Curtis still needs to fix little things like footwork, staying in the pocket and taking care of the football. Curtis has one of the highest turnover worthy play percentages in the SEC, he will put the ball in harms way against this Kentucky defense that has been incredibly opportunistic this season. Curtis does not have much help around him, his offensive line has struggled all season. Vanderbilt allows the highest pressure rate in the SEC, which has led to Curtis being sacked a total of 10 times this season. However, Curtis is really difficult to bring down with his 6'4, 230-pound frame. His ability to erase sack opportunities is similar to South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers. Kentucky will win this matchup in the trenches, this deep defensive line unit will be able to get consistent pressure on Curtis. The biggest question will be how often they can convert those pressures into sacks, which they have been better at doing the last two weeks against Sam Leavitt and John Mateer. It will be a vital coaching point all week for the Wildcats to finish the play and get Curtis on the ground. If they allow Curtis to extend plays with his legs and erase sacks, it can lead to big plays down field as a passer or scrambling for a first down. Luckily for Kentucky, they won't have to see wide receiver Tre Richardson as he transferred to Louisville. Richardson lit them up last year down the field with Diego Pavia throwing all over this defense. I am sure a lot of the returning Wildcats on the defense have not forgotten that 45-17 beatdown last year in Nashville. This motivation will play a factor against a Vanderbilt team that is in a rebuilding stage. The Commodores receiving room is led by veteran Junior Sherrill, who is far and away the best weapon on this offense. Sherrill leads Vanderbilt in receptions, yards and touchdowns. He has four touchdowns on the season and all other wide receivers have combined for just one on the season. This is the guy to watch when Vanderbilt is on offense, they will force feed him the football. Vanderbilt offensive coordinator Tim Beck has one of the most unique offenses in the country and we saw how dangerous it could be last season. However, they lost their quarterback Diego Pavia who thrived in his system, they also lost their mismatch tight end Eli Stowers and the explosive weapon Richardson who transferred to Louisville. This is very much a transition year for this offense and it shows up on film. Kentucky has another opportunity to make a statement on defense after creating four turnovers and holding Oklahoma to just one touchdown last week. Kentucky Football continues to climb in the AP Top 25 Poll , moving up three spots to No. 12 after defeating Oklahoma, 21-13, in Norman. The Wildcats improved to 6-1 overall, became bowl eligible, and strengthened their hopes of reaching the College Football Playoff in head coach Will Stein’s first season. The victory was far from perfect, as Kentucky’s offense struggled to find consistency after an impressive opening drive. However, the defense came up with several crucial plays down the stretch to help the Wildcats secure another impressive road win. Kentucky’s offense looked sharp on its opening possession, slicing through Oklahoma’s defense and setting the tone early. However, the unit stalled after that drive and did not score another offensive touchdown until 12:53 remained in the fourth quarter, when quarterback Kenny Minchey connected with Willie Rodriguez for the Wildcats’ second touchdown of the game. Although the final score was relatively low, Kentucky’s defense also struggled at times in the first half. Safety Jordan Castell came up with a key interception when Oklahoma attempted a fake field goal in the first quarter, ending a promising Sooners possession. The Wildcats’ defense began to turn things around late in the third quarter when Ty Bryant intercepted Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer, giving Kentucky possession in Sooners territory. From there, the defense took control. Oklahoma recorded two three-and-outs and threw two more interceptions. Castell returned one for a pick-six, extending Kentucky’s lead to eight points, while Bryant secured the game-ending interception to seal the victory. While the game was sloppy on both sides, Kentucky found a way to finish strong. The Wildcats improved to 6-1, earned bowl eligibility, and continued building momentum as they pursue a potential College Football Playoff appearance. Now, Kentucky returns home to Kroger Field to face Vanderbilt, looking to avenge consecutive losses to the Commodores while losing three of four in the series. Kentucky fell 45-17 on the road last season after suffering a 20-13 defeat at home the year before. With Vanderbilt struggling through a disappointing season, the Wildcats will have an opportunity to extend their winning ways and continue climbing the national rankings. But if this last weekend showed us anything, it’s that upsets are commonplace this season, and Kentucky can’t afford to come out flat against a Commodores team starving for its first SEC win of the season. That, and Vandy did nearly pull off an upset over an Auburn team that just won at No. 1 Georgia. The Dores may be struggling, but they’ve still got an SEC roster. Vanderbilt Commodores (3-4, 0-4 in SEC) Vanderbilt has struggled through the first seven games of the season, and life after former quarterback Diego Pavia has been challenging. The Commodores finished the 2025 regular season with an impressive 10-2 record before losing to Iowa in the Citrus Bowl, ending the year at 10-3. However, the Dores have not come close to replicating that success this season. Vanderbilt suffered a disappointing 31-21 loss to Arkansas this past weekend. The Razorbacks entered the matchup on a 14-game Southeastern Conference losing streak, but they snapped that drought against the Commodores. One of Vanderbilt’s biggest challenges has been the development of 5-star true freshman quarterback Jared Curtis. The young signal-caller has shown flashes of his talent, but his inexperience has been evident. The drop-off from Pavia to Curtis has been noticeable, and Vanderbilt’s decision to start a true freshman at quarterback has come with growing pains. Through seven games, Curtis has completed 101/161 passes for 62.7%, totaling six passing touchdowns and seven interceptions. He has also been sacked 11 times. Curtis measures 6-foot-3 and weighs 230 pounds, giving him the physical tools to develop into a quality quarterback. He can also make plays with his legs, recording 55 carries for 144 rushing yards and two touchdowns. However, his turnover numbers and struggles under pressure will be areas Kentucky looks to exploit. Vanderbilt’s other major weakness has been its defense, particularly against the run. The Commodores have struggled to establish consistency along their front seven, which could create problems against Kentucky’s rushing attack. The Wildcats have a three-headed backfield featuring CJ Baxter, provided he is healthy enough to play, alongside Jason Patterson and Jovantae Barnes. If Kentucky can keep all three involved, Vanderbilt could have a difficult time slowing down the ground game. Kentucky’s offensive line, known as the Big Blue Wall, has also looked impressive this season. If the unit continues to open running lanes and control the line of scrimmage, the Wildcats could have a significant advantage. As for Vanderbilt’s offense, Curtis has several weapons at his disposal. Senior wide receiver Junior Sherrill has emerged as Curtis’ primary target. The 5-foot-11, 200-pound receiver has recorded 41 receptions for 628 yards and four touchdowns so far this season. Junior wide receiver Ja’Cory Thomas provides another option at 6-foot-3 and 215 pounds. He has recorded 12 receptions for 195 yards and one touchdown. Vanderbilt also features junior tight end Jayvontay Conner, who stands 6-foot-4 and weighs 235 pounds. Conner has totaled 13 receptions for 146 yards, though he has yet to score a touchdown this season. Junior receiver Tristen Brown has added another option in the passing game, recording 12 receptions for 145 yards. In the backfield, Vanderbilt relies primarily on two running backs. Senior Sedrick Alexander, who stands 5-foot-9 and weighs 207 pounds, has recorded 61 carries for 270 yards and five touchdowns. Senior Makhilyn Young, at 5-foot-10 and 210 pounds, has added 52 carries for 216 yards and two touchdowns. For Vanderbilt to pull off the upset, Curtis will need to protect the football, make better decisions under pressure, and find ways to move the ball against Kentucky’s defense. The Commodores will also need to improve against the run to keep the Wildcats’ offense from controlling the game. Kentucky, meanwhile, will look to establish the run early, protect Minchey, and continue creating turnovers defensively. With the Wildcats playing at home and Vanderbilt struggling in SEC play, Kentucky has an opportunity to deliver another convincing win against a team that’s had its number. How to watch Kentucky Wildcats vs. Vanderbilt Commodores Location: Kroger Field — Lexington, Kentucky Time: 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, Oct. 24 TV Info: SEC Network Online Streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening Odds: FanDuel lists Kentucky as an 11.5-point favorite. ESPN gives Kentucky an 85.4% chance of winning. Our Early Prediction: Kentucky enters this matchup at 6-1 and bowl eligible, with its attention now turning toward the College Football Playoff. Under first-year head coach Will Stein, the Wildcats have shown they can win in different ways, whether through explosive offensive performances or clutch defensive plays in lower-scoring games. Vanderbilt, meanwhile, is reeling after falling to 3-4 overall and 0-4 in SEC play. Losing to Arkansas after the Razorbacks had endured a 14-game conference losing streak raises further questions about the direction of the Commodores’ season. Kentucky also has extra motivation after losing to Vanderbilt in each of the past two seasons. With the Wildcats playing at home, an improving defense, and a rushing attack capable of taking control of the game, I expect Kentucky to avenge those losses and earn a convincing victory. It's an interesting matchup for Vegas to predict because USC's strength is the offense and their weakness is their defense. You can basically flip that for Wisconsin, whose defense has been pretty spectacular this season, especially when it comes to scoring defense. But the offense has been rocky at best and putrid at worst. So, the odds feel interesting but pretty close to what you would predict, especially with Wisconsin being the home team and getting to host the USC Trojans. The Badgers look to bounce back against the No. 16 USC Trojans after a momentum-sapping loss against No. 12 UCLA. The Wisconsin football team went into its high-profile Saturday night clash with the University of California Los Angeles Bruins with all the ingredients for a major upset on the hallowed grounds of the Rose Bowl. They were riding a four-game winning streak , bolstered by their dominant defense who were set to take on a backup quarterback, and it looked like the Badgers were primed for a season-defining win in Pasadena. Instead, the Badgers suffered a disappointing 17-7 loss to Bob Chesney’s surging Bruins, and now have another opportunity to break into the AP Top 25 rankings with a win over No. 16 University of Southern California this Saturday night at Camp Randall. If the Badgers want to take advantage of the golden opportunity to display the evolution of their program after a promising start, several key aspects of their play must respectively change or stay the same to dominate the rest of their schedule. Wisconsin is in the midst of a three-game stretch that will determine whether the season will be the bounceback year fans were expecting, amid a funding increase , or just mid-tier bowl eligibility. The following must happen if the Badgers want to score an upset victory over Lincoln Riley’s Trojans this weekend. Keep swinging the hammer on defense Wisconsin’s defense, anchored by the fearsome second-level presence of sophomore linebackers Cooper Catalano and Mason Posa, has been a strong point all season. Through six games, the Badgers have only allowed 16.7 points per game, placing them in the upper echelon of the Big Ten. With regards to Catalano and Posa specifically, the linebacker duo are ranked fifth and 11th respectively in the Big Ten in total tackles. Posa is tied first in the conference for solo tackles, and leads all linebackers. They showed how great they are at run-stopping against UCLA last week and one of the nation’s best running backs in Wayne Knight. Without a doubt, this dangerous duo will have a big part to play if the Badgers hope to halt the potent offense of USC. That objective begins with finding a way to contain Senior Trojan Quarterback Jayden Maiava. Maiava leads the entire Big Ten in passing yards, and is second only to Oregon State’s Braden Atkinson in the entire FBS. Disrupting the offensive rhythm of the Palalo, the Hawaii native will be key to stopping USC’s high-flying offense. This is a huge test for Wisconsin’s secondary, who didn’t have the best showing against UCLA last week, allowing 264 passing yards. USC’s rushing attack also poses a viable second option-threat to a strong Wisconsin run defense. The Trojan backfield is anchored by King Miller, who has averaged 5.2 yards over 114 carries in the Trojans’ first seven games. But make no mistake; this Trojan offense is pass-first and early, and frequent pressure from Catalano, Posa and other defensive stalwarts like Sebastian Cheeks and Charles Perkins will go a long way in damaging the effectiveness of the Trojan offense. Pair that with the potential short fields created by the cannon leg of Badger punter Sean West — who has the fourth longest punt in the Big Ten this year at 70 yards — and the Badger defense has a real chance to impact Maiava and the USC offense. The offense has to seize opportunity To give him credit where it’s due, Colton Joseph has much improved in his ability to take care of the football. The senior quarterback has not recorded a turnover since his three-interception rollercoaster performance against Penn State in Happy Valley. More is required of Joseph in terms of passing the ball, however: he recorded a season-low woeful 66 yards passing in last week’s loss. That level of play did not cut it against the Bruins in Pasadena, and another lackluster performance could mean a long night on Saturday against the Trojans. A victory against Top 20 opposition like the Trojans will demand a well-rounded performance from Joseph, and the Badgers offense as a whole. Joseph has been using his capable running ability — rushing for 333 yards so far this season , with a season high 141 against Michigan State. Joseph could see greater success against USC, however, if the Badgers are able to diversify their ground game by utilizing capable running backs Darrion Dupree and Abu Sama, and by being fundamentally sound blocking the run. On the whole, the name of the game for the Wisconsin offense on Saturday night is diversity. The Badgers should aim to split their play calling between design runs for Joseph, strong running back play from Dupree and Sama, and screen passes blocked well by the offensive line to attack USC. The Trojan defense is far from the best the Badgers will face all year. The Trojans have allowed their opponents 25.1 points on average this year, only .3 less than Michigan State, who Wisconsin dominated handily on homecoming. If the Badgers can at all replicate the offensive success they had against the Spartans, they will make life very difficult for the Trojans. Maximize the environment and rattle them early The temperature in Madison on Saturday night at the 6:30 kickoff time will be around 67°F, with temperatures dropping into the high 50s as the game continues . While not quite cold enough to freeze out the Californians, it has all the makings of a great night at Camp Randall. The crowd will have a huge role to play in this game, packing Camp Randall and fueling the on-field Badgers with their cheers. If the defense is able to suffocate the Trojans early, getting the crowd involved will put the wind at the back of the Badgers and give them a significant boost. Crowd noise on crucial third downs for the Trojan offense could hinder communication, and strong stops by the Badger defense on those plays could give the offense the juice it needs to make a strong start to this game. Starting fast on offense will also embolden the Badger faithful; if Joseph and the Wisconsin offense are able to get down the field quickly and potentially pick up an early score, it’ll energize what is sure to be a great crowd on a beautiful fall evening in Madison. Saturday’s game is more than just another opportunity against ranked opposition in what is a string of them for Wisconsin. It’s a chance, in front of a raucous home crowd, to prove their off-season efforts and early-season success can translate into primetime wins against the Big Ten’s elite. If they fail once again, questions regarding Coach Luke Fickell’s future in Madison could arise once more. The Badgers have the ingredients to upset the Trojans, but whether they can pull it off will be a major indicator in what the Badgers will look like throughout the rest of the regular season. UCLA has already announced that quarterback Nico Iamaleava, safety Tao Johnson, wide receivers Mikey Matthews and Jonah Smith and offensive lineman Sam Yoon will all be out for Saturday's game. Cornerback Rodrick Pleasant, offensive lineman Jordan Davis and defensive lineman Ashton Sanders are all questionable for the Bruins. The injuries aren't too much of a surprise, with it being reported earlier this week that Iamaleava will be forced to miss the rest of the 2026 season with a leg injury. Matthews has also been reported as out for the season , meaning offensive coordinator Dean Kennedy will be without two pieces of his offense for the rest of the year. Here’s a New Mexico vs North Dakota State prediction. We will look at this from a betting perspective and determine the best New Mexico vs North Dakota State pick. North Dakota State Bison Betting Preview The Bison have been on a pretty good run this year so far; they’ve only got one blemish on the schedule. North Dakota State opened with wins over Jacksonville State, Fordham, Air Force, Sacramento State and Wyoming. The lone loss this year came on October 10 versus UNLV, but the Bison recovered with a win over Nevada last weekend for a 6-1 overall record. In the Nevada game, the Bison fell behind 11-0 in the second quarter but then rattled off three straight touchdowns for a 19-11 halftime lead. North Dakota State added a few more scores from there for a 31-17 victory in the end. QB Nathan Hayes was 19-of-25 for 153 yards and two touchdowns . Jackson Williams caught five balls for 58 yards in the victory. New Mexico Lobos Betting Preview Over on the Lobos’ side, they also have just one blemish on their schedule so far. New Mexico beat Central Michigan and Mercyhurst in their first two games ahead of a tough 14-6 loss to Oklahoma. The Lobos have since been on a tear, taking out New Mexico State, UTEP and Hawaii over the last three games on the way to a 5-1 overall run. Matched up against Hawaii last weekend the Lobos were down 10-0 by the end of the first half. New Mexico began their comeback with a TD in the third, then added two more trips to the end zone on the way to a 21-10 victory in the end. QB Toa Fa’avae was 5-of-10 for 59 yards and two picks. Scottre Humphrey had 15 carries for 90 yards and two scores. New Mexico vs North Dakota State Prediction I’ll stick with New Mexico but you could call this one either way. The Lobos played an ugly game versus Hawaii, bagging three turnovers and 16 penalties for 145 yards. New Mexico mustered just 94 yards passing, 5-of-13 on third downs and 16 first downs but the defense kept the team from imploding with 3-of-13 on third downs and two takeaways. New Mexico has 21 or more points in all five of their wins this year and 38 or more in four of them. As for North Dakota State, they held Nevada to just 15 first downs and 286 total yards with two takeaways in their latest win. The Bison defense has been great this year, giving up 17 points or fewer in six of seven games. This matchup could go a lot of different ways and it’ll be a fun one to watch. North Dakota State’s Jackson Williams returns missed field goal for insane 100 yard touchdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut Week 7 Fantasy Football Rankings Nick Meyer, ClutchPoints Sun, October 18, 2026 at 5:54 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The North Dakota State Bison welcomed the Nevada Wolfpack to Fargodome in Fargo, North Dakota and won 31-17 in a FBS showdown among two Mountain West teams . Bison coach Tim Polasek is now on a seven-year deal and looking to make a splash in FBS, something his kick returner Jackson Williams was able to do in Week 7. McFadden's 57-yard bomb fell short, giving Williams a chance to work his magic. CBS Sports shared video of the Play of the Year candidate, which helped NDSU open up a solid lead before halftime. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Bison have continued their pursuit of excellence amid their step up in competition as they now sit at 3-1 in the Mountain West Conference, 6-1 overall. Their sterling conference record has them tied with the Air Force Falcons and Wyoming Cowboys for first place in the conference, with more challenges on the horizon for later this season. Week 8 brings a road game against the New Mexico Lobos, followed by a home date with the UTEP Miners in Week 9. A road trip to Hawaii will give Polasek's team a chance to get away from the cold, and will be followed up with games against Northern Illinois and San Jose State to finish the season. College football is now a national sport, and the rise of the Bison has shown how far a program can go with the right vision and the right leadership. Williams' signature play showed that North Dakota State is a team to be reckoned with, and a well-coached team capable of taking advantage of its opportunities on a grand scale. home.headline: New Mexico linebacker Jaxton Eck out for 'a while' after suffering shoulder injury
home.blurb: Multiple Lobos listed as out or questionable for Saturday's game against Hawaii UNM’s Jaxton Eck (6) gets ready for the next play during a scrimmage at University Stadium in Albuquerque NM on August 15, 2026. Mike Sandoval/Journal Sean Reider Sean Reider Journal Staff Writer Published October 15, 2026 - 12:01 p.m. Modified October 15, 2026 - 2:34 p.m. New Mexico linebacker Jaxton Eck will be out for “a while” after breaking a bone in his shoulder, head coach Jason Eck told the Journal on Thursday. The 6-foot-1, 228-pound senior did not practice this week and was observed with his arm in a sling before he was ruled out for Saturday’s game at Hawaii. Jason Eck said the preseason Mountain West Defensive Player of the Year’s bone break is in the same shoulder he hurt in the Rate Bowl on Dec. 27. Eck added that he does not believe Jaxton’s injury is season-ending, but expects him to miss an extended period of time. His designation was first released via an initial availability report from the Mountain West on Thursday, one that saw multiple key Lobos listed as out or questionable ahead of Saturday’s game. Late to seeing this: LB Jaxton Eck and CB Frankie Edwards III are OUT for Saturday’s game. WR Massiah Mingo and RB Kiefer Sibley are also questionable. https://t.co/5jqZVKeiZ5 Only one Lobo was newly ruled out for the rest of the season on the initial report: backup linebacker Nick Wheeler, who Eck said suffered a torn ACL. Without Jaxton and Wheeler, UNM is expected to rely on linebackers Mercury Swaim and Clay Martineau for the near future. Starting cornerback Frankie Edwards III (9 total tackles) has also been ruled out for Saturday’s game, per the league’s availability report. Eck said the 5-10, 178-pound junior suffered a concussion, and expects him to return as soon as next week. Wide receiver Massiah Mingo (ankle) and running back Kiefer Sibley (shoulder) are questionable for Saturday’s game, per the availability report. A 5-9, 170-pound freshman, Mingo has caught five passes for 56 yards; Sibley has rushed for 205 yards, the second-best mark on the team.
